title: Build the boundary test input
prompt: Before the HbA1c step goes into the pipeline, it needs a unit test input that sits on every edge. Each lab sets its own cut-offs, given in the one-row table `cutoffs`. Build the input in `solve(cutoffs)` with `spark.createDataFrame` and return what the starter's `hba1c_band` step gives for it with those cut-offs.
rules: The input has the columns `observation_id` (text), `code` (text) and `value` (double), the ones the step reads.

Six HBA1C results, with ids `T1` to `T6`: 0.1 below `prediabetes_from`, exactly `prediabetes_from`, 0.1 below `diabetes_from` and exactly `diabetes_from` (each side of both cut-offs, to one decimal), a result with no value, and a result whose value is not a number.
hints: `spark.createDataFrame(rows, "observation_id STRING, code STRING, value DOUBLE")` takes a list of tuples and the schema as text; `cutoffs.first()` gives the cut-offs as a Row.
A missing value is `None`. A value that isn't a number is `float("nan")`: Spark keeps it as NaN, which is not the same as NULL.
`5.7 - 0.1` in Python is `5.6000000000000005`: `round(..., 1)` gives 5.6. And `FLOAT` is a smaller type than `DOUBLE`: 5.7 stored as a float isn't exactly 5.7.
explanation: A test input is a small DataFrame you choose: `spark.createDataFrame(rows, "observation_id STRING, code STRING, value DOUBLE")` with one tuple per result. The boundary values sit on each side of both cut-offs, so a `<` written as `<=` would show up; they come from `cutoffs`, so the same test works for every lab, and `round(c.prediabetes_from - 0.1, 1)` keeps 5.6 from becoming 5.6000000000000005. `None` gives the missing value and `float("nan")` gives NaN; they are different values and the step must handle both, so each needs its own row. The schema matters too: as `FLOAT`, 5.7 becomes 5.69999980926…, which is a different test, and as a decimal the step's output no longer has a double `value`. The step gives no band to T5 and T6.
